stem: An average-risk adult for whom colorectal cancer screening is indicated asks whether colonoscopy is the only screening option. Which response by the nurse is accurate?

options.A: Colonoscopy is the only recommended colorectal cancer screening strategy
options.B: Recommended options include stool-based tests and direct-visualization tests such as colonoscopy
options.C: Screening requires a surgical biopsy before any other test can be used
options.D: Stool-based tests are used only after colorectal cancer has already been diagnosed

rationale: The USPSTF lists multiple recommended colorectal cancer screening strategies for average-risk adults, including stool-based tests such as FIT and direct-visualization tests such as colonoscopy, flexible sigmoidoscopy, and CT colonography. Therefore B is accurate. Colonoscopy is not the only recommended strategy, screening does not require surgical biopsy first, and stool tests are screening tools used before a diagnosis is established.
educational_objective: Explain that colorectal cancer screening can be performed with several evidence-based strategies, including stool-based and direct-visualization tests, rather than colonoscopy alone.
source_locator: How to implement this recommendation; Practice Considerations > Screening Tests; Table 1: multiple recommended stool-based and direct-visualization screening strategies are available and clinicians/patients may consider test characteristics and preferences
source_claim_supported: For average-risk adults for whom colorectal cancer screening is indicated, multiple recommended strategies are available, including stool-based tests and direct-visualization tests such as colonoscopy.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p.9 / PDF p.13: perform targeted screening assessments; educate clients about preventive care and health-maintenance recommendations
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — preventive screening education
correction_summary: Replaced the generic ACS citation with the official USPSTF recommendation, specified an average-risk adult for whom screening is indicated, and narrowed the item to the evidence-supported fact that several recommended screening strategies exist. Removed vague 'other options' wording and rebuilt concise distractors without introducing screening intervals or ages that are unnecessary to the construct.
audit_findings: B is directly supported by USPSTF. A incorrectly limits screening to colonoscopy, C confuses screening with diagnostic tissue sampling, and D reverses the role of stool-based screening. The stem avoids age/interval disputes by specifying that screening is already indicated. No second answer, cueing, unsupported precision, or unresolved conflict remains.
